The news: Quantum computing software company Q-CTRL has raised USD290 million ($415 million) at a valuation above USD1 billion in a series C round led by Salesforce Ventures.
The context: Q-CTRL’s products help make quantum computing useful by correcting errors and improving performance. It also builds Ironstone Opal, a quantum positioning system that enables geolocation without the need for GPS. Customers include Lockheed Martin, Airbus and IBM.
The round required two expansions to meet the level of investor demand. Among the new investors is the federal government’s National Reconstruction Fund, which has tipped in $70 million.
Other new investors include Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners and SPARX Asset Management.
Returning investors include Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg.
What they said: “The investor syndicate we’ve assembled showcases the strength of our technology, revenue growth, and strategic alignment with some of the most important sectors today, from AI to aviation,” Q-CTRL CEO and founder Michael Biercuk said.
Salesforce Ventures partner Robert Keith said: “The hard problem in quantum is not building the machine, it is getting useful output from it. Q-CTRL solves that with AI-powered control software, and the proof is already public: a materials simulation on IBM hardware that any developer can now call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight.”
“That software layer will decide whether quantum shows up in enterprise data centers this decade, and it is why Salesforce Ventures led this round,” Keith said.
The sources: Q-CTRL media release , NRF media release

articles.text:
Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:33 PM
Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity
Zilch has increased its securitization and corporate debt facilities by £165 million, bringing total commitments to £395 million as the payments company expands its product offering. Deutsche Bank led the latest financing, with participation from two major credit funds. The facilities will enable Zilch to originate up to £6 billion in lending annually.
The additional capacity supports customer growth and demand for products including Pay Monthly, launched in August 2026. That offering allows qualifying customers to spread purchases over three, six or 12 months.
Zilch is targeting a broader range of spending needs, including larger purchases such as holidays, household appliances and insurance premiums.
Average annual spending per active customer has reached £2,500, while the company’s gross merchandise value run rate has exceeded £3.5 billion.
The financing follows Zilch’s announcement that it surpassed a $300 million annual run rate and recorded two consecutive quarters of adjusted profit before tax in its 2027 financial year.
The company also plans to move into a new London headquarters in spring 2027, more than doubling its office capacity.
Founded in 2018, Zilch combines debit, credit, installments, earned wage access, credit-building features, offers and rewards within its payments platform.
The expanded funding facilities provide more lending capacity as that product mix develops. Management identified access to efficient funding as important to supporting higher transaction volumes and continued growth.
Chief Financial Officer Hugh Courtney said the financing reflects funders’ confidence in Zilch’s underwriting and ability to scale profitably in the United Kingdom.
The company’s strategy is to serve more customer payment needs through the same platform, strengthening engagement as users move between everyday spending and larger purchases.
KEY QUOTES:
“As we continue to grow at significant scale, having access to efficient funding is a key parameter for success. These expanded facilities give us greater capacity to support our customers where they need us, capturing more of the transactions that matter to customers day to day and providing the most rewarding ways to pay. By serving a broader range of customer needs, we can continue building a highly engaged customer relationship and delivering the value, flexibility and features that our customers really want.”
Philip Belamant, CEO And Co-Founder Of Zilch
“We are proud of our close partnerships with our funders, led by Deutsche Bank, who continue to support our growth as we scale the business profitably in the UK. The upsizing of the facilities represents a strong endorsement of our underwriting capabilities, product market fit and ability to continue scaling at pace.”
Hugh Courtney, Chief Financial Officer Of Zilch

articles.title: Exus Closes $345 Million Financing Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives
articles.snippet: Exus Closes $345 Million Financing Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives Hoodline
articles.text:
Source: Nikki / Wikimedia Commons
Exus Renewables North America said Thursday it closed $345 million in senior secured holding company financing led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, money the company says will go toward construction and new U.S. wind, solar and battery projects.
The check is another in a run of company financings and project deals, not a map of which turbines or panels get the cash. Exus framed the close against rising U.S. electricity demand and described itself as an independent owner, developer and operator of utility-scale renewable energy and storage.
What the Money Is For
Exus said the financing will support construction costs and development across its growing U.S. portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets. The announcement does not name the projects that will draw on the facility or split the dollars among those three technologies.
President and CEO Jim Spencer said the financing lets the company keep its momentum going. He also said Goldman Sachs Alternatives' support reflects confidence in Exus and gives it flexibility to build projects and bring generation online, including work already underway and a deeper pipeline.
Vikas Agrawal, managing director and co-head of Energy Transition Climate Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, said Exus has a strong platform for developing and operating utility-scale renewable projects. "We're pleased to support its continued investment in new energy infrastructure," he said, tying that support to growing U.S. electricity demand.
A Larger Company-Reported Book
Exus reported more than 800 megawatts operating or under construction and a total portfolio exceeding 6 gigawatts. Those are company figures, not an outside audit of nameplate capacity.
The comparison that is on the record is Exus' own July 22, 2025 financing announcement. Then, the company reported more than 5 gigawatts in its total portfolio and 764 megawatts operating or under construction, alongside $308.2 million in financing for the 185-megawatt Zia Solar portfolio in New Mexico and the 169-megawatt Keystone wind portfolio in Pennsylvania.
From that July 2025 snapshot to Thursday's release, the company-reported operating-or-under-construction figure moved from 764 megawatts to more than 800, and the total portfolio from over 5 gigawatts to more than 6. Exus also said it is expanding its operational footprint to meet growing national energy needs, with work that includes developing, repowering and managing renewable assets.
Separate Deals, Not One Stack
This holding-company financing sits beside other Exus transactions that the available reporting treats as separate. pv magazine USA reported in January that Exus had closed a $400 million senior secured corporate credit facility tied to a 4.5-gigawatt pipeline. Nothing in the Thursday announcement establishes whether that facility is still outstanding or how it relates to the $345 million.
Project-level money has also moved on its own track. On Sept. 22, Exus said it had completed the Highland North and Cambria wind repower projects in Cambria County, Pennsylvania, and that construction was financed through roughly $356 million led by KeyBanc Capital Markets. A week later, on Sept. 29, Exus and ibV Energy Partners announced that Exus had acquired four solar projects totaling 715 megawatts-peak.

The Institutional Infrastructure Battery Fund (IIBF) is launching as an infrastructure investment fund for institutional investors, specifically focused on large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Germany. At launch, the fund has already secured its first two storage projects in central Germany under purchase agreements and has an identified project pipeline representing an investment volume of more than €300 million.
As renewable energy deployment progresses, large-scale battery storage systems are becoming an important component in stabilizing the German electricity grid and balancing volatile generation peaks. The IIBF translates this structural infrastructure need into an investment profile tailored to regulated institutional investors: the fund invests in a diversified portfolio of large-scale battery storage projects in Germany that are ready to build or close to their commercial operation date (COD) and holds them for the long term following acquisition. Early-stage project development and permitting risks therefore remain outside the fund.
Clearly defined responsibilities: institutional investment management and European energy trading expertise
The IIBF is built on a clearly defined division of responsibilities between two established specialists in their respective markets:
Investment management, underwriting and structuring by 2IP: Institutional Investment Partners (2IP) is responsible for investment management, transaction underwriting and institutional fund structuring. As the storage facilities are held throughout the fund's term, pre-acquisition due diligence is particularly important: 2IP assesses each transaction against clearly defined risk, financial viability and cash flow criteria, incorporates contractual security mechanisms and provides ongoing oversight through its portfolio and investment management.
Market access, asset management, software and energy trading by Second Foundation: As one of Europe's major technology-driven energy traders, the Second Foundation Group manages the energy-related and technological value chain surrounding the storage facilities. This ranges from direct project access and commercial and technical asset management of the facilities, through proprietary control and monitoring software, to high-frequency trading of capacity in the European electricity and balancing markets.
Contractually underpinned base distributions with additional market upside
The IIBF's income model is designed to cushion downside exposure to the volatility typical of electricity markets while also harnessing it for the portfolio. The core of the fund's income consists of long-term contractual usage fees (lease payments) for making the storage facilities available. Contractual advance payments and additional security mechanisms support the predictability of regular distributions to investors.

articles.title: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going?
articles.snippet: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going? Techli
articles.text:
Four of six deals are reported in Chicago, and the region is experiencing the latest funding activity in the form of investments in AI infrastructure and financial services.
According to StartMidwest’s funding roundup , $213.5 million was raised in six deals by Midwest startups and financial technology companies during the week ending Nov. 6, with two $100 million rounds accounting for almost all the capital.
Ocient, an AI infrastructure firm in Chicago, and Erebor Bank, which is based in Columbus, Ohio, were the leaders of the activity. The remaining included health care technology, artificial intelligence and fintech firms, reflecting the diversity of sectors that are being invested in all over the region.
The headline figure, however, requires some qualification: Erebor Bank’s $100 million investment from Japan’s SBI Holdings was announced as a planned commitment, not a completed financing round. The difference is important in evaluating the amount of capital that actually has flowed to companies in the Midwest.
The biggest round up to date was Ocient’s $100 million Series C , which was announced on November 5. The investment, led by BOKA Capital and OCA Ventures, totals $260 million for the Chicago firm. Other investors who were on board included existing investors Greycroft, In-Q-Tel, Blue Bear Capital, Buoyant Ventures, PSP Growth, Pritzker Group Venture Capital and Eron Wolf. Dallas Venture Capital joined as a new investor.
Ocient is a company that creates data analytics and AI solutions for enterprises dealing with vast amounts of data. The new investment will allow it to continue developing its OcientAIQ solutions that enable enterprises to deploy AI agents and analytics in petabyte-scale data environments.
Reliable, governed data is becoming a key infrastructure need as businesses delve into agentic AI systems that can analyze information and execute tasks. Ocient claims its solution can be used for data governance along with high-performance data analytics, enabling AI agents and analysts to ask questions about the data in a customer’s environment.
The company anticipates that its revenue will more than triple in 2026 due to the demand of customers with growing and high-volume data sets. This projection is not a financial result but an estimate by Ocient.
The second $100 million was from a digital bank called Erebor Bank, based in Columbus, Ohio, which offers services to companies in fields such as artificial intelligence, robotics and advanced manufacturing, defense, and energy. The timing of the completion of the investment was not mentioned in the funding roundup, but SBI Holdings revealed its plan to invest $100 million .
Four of the six transactions were in Chicago. In addition to Ocient, medical technology firm Focused Medical Technologies, a treatment developer for pulmonary embolism, secured $6 million in investment, including two medical technology strategic investors and UCM Ventures. The University of Chicago startup is targeting the funds for product development, manufacturing and setting up for a pivotal study in the United States.
Consumer insights firm QualSights raised $5 million in funding, led by Duo Partners. The company employs smart sensors and a consumer application and AI analytics to provide a better understanding of how humans use physical products. The funding came with the appointment of Prasanna Pitale as Chief Executive.

Asset Based Lending Announces Fourth Securitization of $200 Million, Marking Largest Transaction to Date
News provided by
Asset Based Lending, LLC
Nov 12, 2026, 13:33 ET
Share this article

JERSEY CITY, N.J. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Asset Based Lending (ABL) , a national private lender and a driving force behind the next generation of real estate investment, has successfully closed its fourth unrated securitization, totaling $200 million. The transaction, ABL 2026 RTL-1, which priced on October 15 and closed on October 26, marks ABL's largest to date, bringing its cumulative securitization volume to $723 million.
The transaction is backed by a diversified pool of business-purpose residential real estate loans, with an industry-leading concentration of ground-up infill construction loans. This reflects ABL's 16 years of experience in ground-up construction lending and its proven ability to manage the complexities and risks of residential development.
"We are proud to lead the industry in financing ground-up construction, and to do it at a cost that keeps our pricing competitive for the builders we serve," said Kevin Rodman, CEO of ABL. "This transaction underscores the strength of the platform our team has built and the confidence investors have in our credit. Every one of these loans puts new housing on the ground."
The transaction also demonstrates ABL's ability to navigate challenging market conditions. Despite heightened volatility and increased investor selectivity across the securitization market, ABL secured competitive financing terms. The deal reached the market in approximately three weeks, making it one of the company's fastest securitization executions.
Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC served as structuring agent, with Nomura Securities International, Inc. ("Nomura") and Mizuho Securities USA LLC serving as joint bookrunners.
"Successfully executing this transaction amid market volatility reinforces the effectiveness of our capital markets strategy and the quality of our platform," said Daniel Gotay, Head of Capital Markets at ABL. "We have built durable relationships with institutional investors and established a track record they can underwrite, giving us consistent access to capital. For our borrowers, that is what matters most: they can count on ABL to fund their projects from start to finish."
The securitization also reflects ABL's expanding national footprint, with collateral spanning the Northeast, Sun Belt, Rust Belt and South. This geographic diversification supports the company's strategy to continue growing beyond its established Northeast presence and finance residential development in markets across the country.
To learn more about ABL, please visit www.ablfunding.com .
About Asset Based Lending
Asset Based Lending was established in 2010, providing fast bridge financing to real estate investors for the purchase, renovation, new construction, and long-term refinance of single-family, multi-family, and mixed-use properties. A trusted lender to thousands of investors, Asset Based Lending has closed over $4.4 billion in loans since its founding. Learn more at https://www.ablfunding.com/ . Follow the company on LinkedIn .
